publications.title: SiKS: An Integrated Web-Based Student Counseling Information System with Automated WhatsApp Notifications
publications.abstract: Fragmented school counseling records can obscure case histories, disrupt follow-up, and weaken communication with families. This study developed and formatively evaluated SiKS, an integrated web-based student counseling information system that connects counseling activities through role-based access and automated WhatsApp notifications. Requirements were elicited through interviews with the Vice-Principal for Student Affairs and a School Counselor at an Indonesian vocational high school, supplemented by analysis of the existing workflow. Developed using the Waterfall model, Laravel, and MySQL, the prototype links appointment requests, scheduling, counseling records, follow-up actions, parental summons, reporting, and notification logs across six user roles. Evaluation included 50 black-box scenarios derived from the requirements and user acceptance testing with 20 role-representative respondents after a guided walkthrough. Three validators reviewed the 15-item instrument, assigning 211 out of 225 possible points (93.78%). All 50 executed functional scenarios produced the expected outputs. User acceptance scores totaled 1,336 out of 1,500 points (89.07%), with item scores ranging from 82% to 96%. Interface attractiveness, suitability for school use, menu accessibility, and perceived confidentiality under role-based access received the strongest ratings; report clarity, printing and downloading, and notification services received comparatively lower ratings. The study presents a context-specific design that links case continuity, differentiated access, and event-triggered communication within a single counseling workflow. The findings support functional conformance under the tested conditions and favorable initial user perceptions. Developer-led testing, the single-school setting, and guided exposure limit inferences about independent use, sustained adoption, privacy protection, and counseling outcomes.

publications.title: Course Recommendation System Using Machin Learning
publications.abstract: Abstract Today, many online educational platforms offer a large number of courses, which creates confusion for students while choosing the right course. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a simple and effective hybrid Course Recommendation System using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing. The system combines two main techniques: Content-Based Filtering and Popularity-Based Filtering. In Content-Based Filtering, tools like TF-IDF, Count Vectorizer and Cosine Similarity are used to match course details with student interests. In Popularity-Based Filtering, courses are selected based on top subscriber count and positive user reviews. The backend is built using Python Flask with a clear user interface for easy navigation. The system was tested with multiple machine learning algorithms, where the Decision Tree model achieved the highest accuracy of 90%. Overall, this system helps students quickly find useful courses without wasting time.

publications.title: EXPRESS: Revitalizing the Grocery Store Experience: An Empirical Study on the Spillover Effects of Experiential Services
publications.abstract:
Grocery retailers increasingly use experiential services to attract customers to their stores. However, it remains unclear whether these services generate positive
                    spillover
                    effects to core grocery sales or cannibalize existing demand. We provide the first empirical evidence by studying a grocery retailer that introduced a taphouse as its first experiential service and examining the underlying mechanisms.
                  
                  
                    We combine store transaction records with SafeGraph's point-of-interest data and survey data on product attributes. Using a quasi-experimental design, we specify a synthetic difference-in-differences estimator with staggered treatment timings. Our results show significant positive spillover effects. On average, stores that feature a taphouse experienced a 5.97% increase in daily sales volume, a 6.82% rise in sales revenue, a 5.76% increase in transactions, and a 6.18% expansion in product variety compared to stores without a taphouse. Our mechanism analyses suggest that these results are associated with activity through both
                    extensive
                    (newly observed customers) and
                    intensive
                    (greater purchasing activity among existing customers) margins. We find that an average order contains fewer but relatively higher-priced items, leaving average order value statistically unchanged. Newly acquired customers make relatively smaller purchases than existing customers, whose order size does not change significantly following the taphouse introduction. We also find that products complementary to the taphouse and those with a greater propensity for impulse purchasing account for larger shares of grocery sales following taphouse introduction. Finally, nearby competing supermarkets experience reductions in both total visits and unique visitors, suggesting that local competitive substitution may contribute to the observed customer expansion.
                  
                  To assess generalizability, we replicate the analysis with another grocery chain in a different region that introduced a full restaurant and obtain qualitatively similar results. Overall, the findings indicate that adding a taphouse can effectively increase grocery sales volume and revenue. Although high setup costs may deter adoption, our break-even analysis projects recovery in approximately 34 to 39 weeks from grocery-side gross-margin contributions alone, or 27 to 44 weeks when alternative assumptions about taphouse profitability, including operating losses, are incorporated.

publications.title: Theoretical lower bounds for a parallel batch scheduling problem
publications.abstract:
Abstract
                  The Oven Scheduling Problem (OSP) is an NP-hard real-world parallel batch scheduling problem arising in the semiconductor industry. Its objective is to schedule a set of jobs on ovens while minimizing total oven runtime, job tardiness, and setup costs. At the same time, it must adhere to various constraints such as oven eligibility and availability, job release dates, setup times between batches, and oven capacity limitations. In this paper, we develop theoretical, problem-specific lower bounds for the OSP that can be computed very quickly. We thoroughly examine these lower bounds, evaluating their quality and capability to improve existing solution methods. Moreover, these problem-specific lower bounds enable us to assess the solution quality for large instances for which exact methods often fail to provide tight lower bounds.

publications.title: AI Hallucinations
publications.abstract: Artificial Intelligence has really transformed areas like healthcare, legal services, education, finance, and business. But its quick spread also brings persistent tech troubles, mainly the confusing issue of AI mistakes, errors, and misinformation. Large Language Models (LLMs) can handle all sorts of tasks, from text creation and code writing to answering questions and summarizing info. Still, despite their big achievements, LLMs sometimes spout incorrect stuff – factually wrong or made-up content – which is called "hallucination." This paper dives deep into AI failures, showing how they differ based on errors in logic, generated fiction presented confidently, and correct data being misinterpreted. It looks at why AI systems act overly sure of themselves, how messy training data messes up, and ideas for fixing this like boosted retrieval methods, cleaner training data, and humans checking the work. What stands out is that these glitches aren't just random tech snafus. Instead, they're a design quirk of big AI language models. Fixing them demands teamwork from folks in various fields, not just developers. So, while there are big issues, figuring out ways to collaborate could make these systems way more reliable in the future.

publications.title: ИНСТИТУЦИОНАЛЬНЫЙ ТИП ВУЗА КАК ФАКТОР ТРАНСФОРМАЦИИ НОРМ ИНТЕРНЕТ-КОММУНИКАЦИИ В ОБРАЗОВАТЕЛЬНОМ ДИСКУРСЕ
publications.abstract: ИНСТИТУЦИОНАЛЬНЫЙ ТИП ВУЗА КАК ФАКТОР ТРАНСФОРМАЦИИ НОРМ ИНТЕРНЕТ-КОММУНИКАЦИИ В ОБРАЗОВАТЕЛЬНОМ ДИСКУРСЕ Цель исследования – выявить особенности цифровой образовательной коммуникации студентов и преподавателей в зависимости от институционального типа вуза и социокультурных характеристик учебных групп. Материал исследования составили около 500 сообщений из 20 Telegram-чатов Узбекского государственного университета мировых языков и Университета Alfraganus за период с сентября 2025 года по июль 2026 года. Использованы описательный, сопоставительный, контекстуально-прагматический и количественный методы. Установлено, что в государственном вузе чаще используются формализованные обращения и стратегии поддержания академической дистанции, тогда как в частном университете заметнее сочетание официального и разговорного стилей, сокращений, эмодзи и англицизмов. По результатам анкетирования, 93,1 % респондентов назвали Telegram основным средством образовательной коммуникации, а 78,6 % считают соблюдение сетевого этикета обязательным. Сделан вывод о формировании гибридной модели академического общения, объединяющей традиционные нормы и современные цифровые практики. Ключевые слова: цифровая коммуникация, образовательный дискурс, сетевой этикет, академическая дистанция, высшее образование, социокультурные факторы, Telegram. Tadqiqot materiallarini 2025-yil sentabrdan 2026-yil iyulgacha faoliyat yuritgan O‘zbekiston davlat jahon tillari universiteti va Alfraganus universitetining 20 ta Telegram guruhi hamda 500 ga yaqin xabar tashkil etdi. Tadqiqotda tavsifiy, qiyosiy, kontekstual-pragmatik va miqdoriy metodlardan foydalanildi. Natijalar davlat universiteti guruhlarida rasmiy murojaatlar va akademik masofani saqlash usullari, xususiy universitetda esa rasmiy va so‘zlashuv uslublari uyg‘unligi, qisqartmalar, emojilar va inglizcha o‘zlashmalarning ko‘proq qo‘llanishini ko‘rsatdi. So‘rovnoma natijalariga ko‘ra, respondentlarning 93,1 foizi Telegramni asosiy ta’limiy muloqot vositasi deb hisoblaydi, 78,6 foizi tarmoq odobiga rioya qilishni zarur deb biladi. Raqamli akademik muloqotda an’anaviy me’yorlar va zamonaviy kommunikativ usullar uyg‘unlashayotgani aniqlandi. Kalit so‘zlar: raqamli muloqot, ta’limiy diskurs, tarmoq odobi, akademik masofa, oliy ta’lim, sotsiomadaniy omillar, Telegram. THE INSTITUTIONAL TYPE OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTION AS A FACTOR IN THE TRANSFORMATION OF INTERNET COMMUNICATION NORMS IN EDUCATIONAL DISCOURSE The study aims to identify the features of digital educational communication between students and teachers in relation to the institutional type of higher education institution and the sociocultural characteristics of academic groups. The empirical material consists of approximately 500 messages from 20 Telegram chats at the Uzbekistan State World Languages University and Alfraganus University, collected between September 2025 and July 2026. Descriptive, comparative, contextual-pragmatic, and quantitative methods were applied. The findings indicate that formal forms of address and strategies for maintaining academic distance are more common in the state university, while the private university demonstrates a greater combination of formal and informal registers, abbreviations, emojis, and English borrowings. According to the survey, 93.1% of respondents identified Telegram as their primary educational communication tool, while 78.6% considered compliance with netiquette essential. The study concludes that a hybrid model of academic communication is emerging, combining traditional norms with contemporary digital practices. Keywords: digital communication, educational discourse, netiquette, academic distance, higher education, sociocultural factors, Telegram.

publications.title: International Digital Hajj and Umrah Verification and Protection System: Online Service Model Based on Digital Identity, Dynamic or Code, Digital Holographic Authentication, and Cross-Border Pilgrim Verification
publications.abstract: The organization of Hajj and Umrah is facing new developments due to digital transformation, increased cross-border mobility, the need to protect pilgrims, and demands for service transparency. The third amendment to Law Number 8 of 2019 through Law Number 14 of 2025 explicitly places technological advancements, the dynamics of Hajj and Umrah management at both national and international levels, and the need to improve guidance, services, and protection for pilgrims as part of the considerations for legal changes. On the other hand, Saudi Arabia has developed the Nusuk Hajj digital platform, which allows prospective pilgrims to create accounts, upload documents, fill out applications, go through verification, choose categories, top up e-wallets, select service providers, book packages, and review itineraries digitally. This situation shows that the digitalization of Hajj management has evolved from merely providing information to becoming an integrated digital service and transaction mechanism.This community service proposal develops the International Digital Hajj and Umrah Verification and Protection System (IDHUVPS) model as an additional layer of protection that connects pilgrim identities, document verification, dynamic QR codes, digital holographic authentication, health protection, payments, verification of Hajj and Umrah proxies, complaints, as well as Indonesia–Saudi Arabia data interoperability. This model is not meant to bypass visa requirements, quotas, permits, or applicable Sharia regulations, but is designed as a digital governance model that can be developed through collaboration among authorities

publications.title: AI-Driven Generative Content & Predictive Analytics in Hybrid Academic Libraries: A Zero-Trust, Anti-Deviance Architecture
publications.abstract: Abstract Academic libraries are undergoing a profound paradigm shift, evolving from passive hybrid repositories into autonomous, AI-augmented knowledge ecosystems. While traditional hybrid frameworks address basic print-digital coexistence, they suffer from critical vulnerabilities: high-demand resource friction, physical material mutilation, licensing piracy, unauthorized access, and algorithmic bias in digital discovery. This paper introduces a novel operational paradigm—the Zero-Trust Anti-Deviance Architecture (ZT-ADA)—that integrates Generative AI, Predictive Anomaly Detection, and Dynamic Resource Orchestration (DRO). Under ZT-ADA, predictive models anticipate resource surges during peak evaluation cycles, pre-allocating dynamic multi-user digital access and personalized generative summaries to mitigate physical collection stress. Simultaneously, a zero-trust cyber-physical verification matrix continuously evaluates access telemetry to detect physical deviance (mutilation, concealment, retention abuse) and digital breach threats in real time. We present mathematical formulations, operational workflows, risk matrices, and empirical evaluation metrics to establish a resilient, ethical, and scalable blueprint for 21st-century academic libraries.

publications.title: EXPRESS: The Role of Ease-of-Return Experience on Contingent Free Shipping Policies
publications.abstract:
Contingent free shipping (CFS) policies, whereby consumers get free shipping if their orders exceed a certain amount, are commonplace. Such a policy aims to nudge customers to place larger orders by adding additional items and/or buying more expensive items (
                    order-swelling
                    ). A less desirable possible outcome is that customers pad their orders to avoid paying the shipping fee but later return the opportunistic or impulse-purchase items (
                    return-swelling
                    ). A retailer designing the CFS policy’s terms—threshold and shipping fee—should balance these competing effects. We study how the retailer's return environment, specifically the ease-of-return experience (EOR) for customers, moderates order-swelling or return-swelling behavior induced by a CFS policy.
                  
                  We collaborate with an online fashion retailer that switched across multiple CFS policies over time and offered home pickup of returns in some markets but not in others. Our difference-in-differences empirical strategy builds on these policy switches and the location-based variation in the EOR. We find that the EOR can considerably impact the relative profit performance of the CFS policies and that it moderates both the order-swelling and the return-swelling responses. Our counterfactual analysis reveals that return-swelling is the key driver of the observed difference in the relative profit performance of CFS policies across the two EOR market types.
                  Our study documents a novel determinant of the financial performance of a CFS policy: the ease-of-return experience. Our analysis indicates that our collaborating retailer would be better off selecting a (relatively) lenient CFS policy in more convenient EOR markets and a (relatively) stringent CFS policy in less convenient EOR markets.

publications.title: Gretchen Andrew on Hacking Google With Vision Boards | NFTS.WTF Interview
publications.abstract: Artist Gretchen Andrew on the vision boards she uses to manipulate search algorithms, how NFTs make the digital side of her practice collectible, and why she wants smart contracts to reward the people behind her career.Interviewed by David Cash. Book David to host, moderate, or speak: https://davidcash.ca Recorded in December 2021 during Art Basel Miami Beach, Gretchen and David Cash, who met through a Unit London NFT show that also involved Kenny Schachter, talk about how she gets her drawn vision boards to the top of Google for searches like "contemporary art auction record." She explains leaving a job at Google to become an artist, teaching workshops on internet literacy, and making NFT glitch GIFs whose first frame is the only part Google reads. She also previews CV NFTs, badges for past and future career achievements, and her plan to write gallery contracts in Solidity.
